what: Sasol turns coal and gas into liquid fuels and chemicals. Its Secunda plant in South Africa makes a large share of the country's petrol and diesel from coal, and it sells specialty chemicals worldwide.
customers: South African fuel buyers, and chemical customers in Europe, Asia and North America.
money: synthetic fuels, gas and mining in South Africa
specialty and commodity chemicals in Africa, America and Eurasia
moat: The Secunda coal-to-liquids plant is unique in the world: nobody else operates this technology at scale, and it supplies a large share of South Africa's transport fuel.
risks: Coal-to-liquids is extremely carbon-intensive, which brings regulatory and financing pressure
South African electricity, rail and port problems all constrain operations
opportunities: 10.5 times earnings and 3.3 times EBITDA with $671M of free cash flow
Revenue recovered to $15.7B over the last twelve months
Only one analyst covers it, and that target implies about 69% upside
watch: Secunda production volumes and the rand oil price.
